title: Balkrishna Industries Ltd-$ - 502355 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Volumes strong but margins squeezed by raw-material and freight inflation; EBITDA margin fell to 18.24% in Q2 with price hikes of 2-3% only partly passing through; capex ~INR 1,850 crores spent in H1, with remainder spread over two years.

summary.headline: Balkrishna Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 49% YoY to INR 3,450 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 18.24% on raw material and freight inflation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue was INR 3,450 crore (up 49% YoY, after INR 41 crore realised FX loss) with EBITDA of INR 629 crore at 18.24% margin and PAT of INR 291 crore. H1 revenue was INR 6,859 crore (up 35%), H1 EBITDA INR 1,332 crore (19.42% margin) and H1 PAT INR 723 crore. Management said raw material and freight inflation hit profitability and would persist for the next few quarters, with only partial pass-through through 2-3% price hikes mainly in India. The company also announced a Pirelli offtake tie-up for premium PCR tyres at its Bhuj facility, with a possible 50-50 JV for a second phase.

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,887 crore (gross debt INR 5,985 crore, cash INR 3,100 crore)

segments.name: Off-highway tyres (OHT)
segments.commentary: Good sales volume growth in Q2, helped by a low base in the US (tariff-hit last year). Europe faced weather and agricultural headwinds, India outperformed, and the Americas were stable. The All-Steel Radial mining range is gaining acceptance.

segments.name: On-road (TBR, 2-wheeler, upcoming PCR)
segments.commentary: Contributed low single-digit percent of Q2 sales volume and is part of the 'others' 8,000-ton bucket. PCR launch is planned for January 2027. Management targets 5% market share and 20% of turnover from the new vertical by 2030.

segments.name: Carbon black
segments.commentary: Decent YoY revenue growth in Q2; third-party sales are about 10% of the business. Capex is complete and the new line will mainly serve external customers, with a roadmap toward specialty blacks.

guidance_outlook: Raw material and freight inflation expected to continue for the next few quarters; no quantum given for the commodity impact in Q2 or the Q3 outlook.
Price hikes of about 2-3% taken mainly in India; further price increases to be a tactical mix of price and volume, quantum not shared.
Capex on track at about INR 3,000 crore for the year; the remaining spend is to be done over the next two years.
Pirelli Phase 1 PCR production and sales to start in the next calendar year, ramping to 8 lakh tyres by year four (2030).
Management aims to sustain the roughly 90,000 metric ton quarterly run rate but would not commit to a number.
Second interim dividend of INR 4 per share declared, in addition to INR 4 paid for Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR 1,850 crore; full-year plan of about INR 3,000 crore stated as on track.
Carbon black: all capex complete and the new line recently came online; the old capacity was fully utilised, and the new line is to be filled mainly with third-party sales.

Pirelli offtake at Bhuj for premium PCR tyres: Phase 1 production starts next calendar year, with a possible second phase as a 50-50 JV, subject to conditions, for a dedicated plant serving India and export markets.
Preponed capex by a couple of quarters to speed up project completion, which was funded partly by new borrowing.
demand_pricing: Demand volatile due to geopolitics; Q2 volumes grew well YoY, though Q2 FY26 was depressed by US tariffs.
Europe faced extreme weather and agricultural pressure; the company says it is growing in all major European countries.
India: positive trends across all micro-markets despite erratic monsoons; India share of volumes rose to about 40%, which slightly hurt margin.
Carbon black raw material costs are volatile, driven by higher crude prices.
Inventory build partly due to supply-chain disruption and stocking ahead of the EUDR regulation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ~90,000 MT quarterly volume run rate sustain in H2, given the low US base and growth in Europe, the Americas and India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not comment on a specific number but said it will endeavour to hit those levels and maximise sales and revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much was the Q2 commodity inflation impact, and what price was taken and planned for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity impact not disclosed. About 2-3% price increase taken, mainly in India; global pricing will be a tactical mix of price and volume.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material cost rose about 17% QoQ; will there be further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost pressure to continue for a couple of quarters; no price quantum shared, with a judicious price-volume balance to be used.

qa_highlights.question: Freight cost level and whether it is being passed through in ASP?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight about 6.5% of sales value; sea freight expected at elevated levels with a marginal rise, and freight is not yet passed through in ASP.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 'BKT 2.0' split of carbon black and tyres a separate P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: No; it is for marketing and branding only. It is one company with three areas (off-road, on-road, carbon) under Vision 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Europe volumes not fall QoQ, and is the trend sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said to look at YoY growth, which was substantial; QoQ numbers were marginally lower due to supply-chain and freight issues.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital build and rise in debt: is it capex-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital rose in line with H1 revenue growth of 35%, and inventory rose on supply-chain disruption and EUDR stocking; debt rose because capex was preponed by a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 carried the promotion spend for the Indian T20 league (IPL), booked in full in that quarter, so the seasonal pattern should recur.

risks_watch: Raw material and freight inflation expected to persist for several quarters, with only partial pass-through so far.
Gross margin per kg and the cost trajectory were not guided; management declined to comment on the analyst's INR 160-165 estimate.
Net debt rose to INR 2,887 crore after heavy capex and working capital build; monitor deleveraging.
Ramp-up risk for new verticals: PCR launch in January 2027 and Pirelli Phase 1 next calendar year.
Europe demand weakness due to weather and agriculture, plus EUDR-related inventory levels.
Mix shift toward India (about 40% of volume) and away from the US may weigh on margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth and long-term vision, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins, pricing and cost. Management repeatedly declined to quantify commodity impact, price hikes or gross margin per kg, citing forward-looking constraints.
key_quotes: The profitability was impacted due to the headwinds caused by inflation in raw materials and freight costs.
Going forward, we believe these headwinds will continue in the coming few quarters.
This strategic tie-up not only fills our capacity but also strongly establishes our position as a commendable player in the Indian premium PCR market.
So the channel, the inventory is at normal levels, so that is what it is.

adds.what: Carbon black new line (third-party sales focus), capex complete and recently commissioned
Pirelli offtake Phase 1 PCR production at Bhuj facility, starting next calendar year (Jan 2027 PCR launch), ramping to 8 lakh tyres by 2030

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management guides a 20-25% long-term EBITDA margin endeavour and a Pirelli PCR ramp to 8 lakh tyres by 2030, with capex of about INR 3,000 crore for the year on track (INR 1,850 crore spent in H1), while Q2 revenue rose 49% YoY and H1 35%, mainly on a low US base and India share gains.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 18.24% in Q2 FY27 (H1 19.42%) as raw material costs rose about 17% QoQ and freight is about 6.5% of sales, with management saying inflation persists for a couple of quarters and only 2-3% price hikes taken so far.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Carbon black new line already commissioned and Pirelli Phase 1 PCR production at Bhuj starts next calendar year (PCR launch January 2027) toward 8 lakh tyres by 2030; capex of about INR 3,000 crore for FY27 is on track with INR 1,850 crore spent in H1.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 standalone revenue rose 49% YoY and H1 volume was 185,167 MT, with management aiming to sustain about 90,000 MT per quarter, though it would not commit to a number and Europe was marginally lower QoQ.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: A possible 50-50 JV for a second Pirelli phase at a dedicated plant is subject to conditions, and the remaining capex is being spent over the next two years; no new board-approved project was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue guidance was given, and management declined to quantify margin, commodity impact or gross margin per kg, so there is no basis for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects raw material and freight inflation to persist for a couple of quarters with no quantum given, and freight is not yet passed through in ASP, so margin guidance risk remains.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PCR launch is planned for January 2027 with Pirelli Phase 1 production starting next calendar year, both already under way.

rows.label: Further price hikes on raw material pass-through
rows.why: About 2-3% price hike taken mainly in India so far, with further tactical price-volume moves planned but quantum not shared, while raw material rose about 17% QoQ.

rows.label: Pirelli offtake tie-up for premium PCR at Bhuj
rows.why: Offtake tie-up is signed with Phase 1 production starting next calendar year and ramping to 8 lakh tyres by 2030.

rows.label: Second interim dividend INR 4 per share
rows.why: INR 4 per share declared, in addition to INR 4 paid for Q1 FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume growth, the Pirelli PCR ramp and the long-term 20-25% margin endeavour, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins, commodity impact and pricing; analysts pressed on the Q3 price hike quantum, commodity impact and freight pass-through.
